fix(admin): payouts manual joins, escrow read-only view, inline bank account form

- Rewrote /api/admin/payouts GET to use manual batch queries instead of
  PostgREST nested joins -- payment_requests has no FK constraints so
  the aliased join syntax returned nothing; now fetches agreements,
  profiles, bank accounts, and emails in parallel then merges them

- Repurposed admin escrow page as a read-only financial overview:
  removed the release-payment button, added status badges (Payment held /
  Awaiting approval / Awaiting payout), summary strip with total held and
  per-status counts, and expanded the API query to include paid_held and
  delivered agreements alongside completed ones; renamed nav tab to Funds

- Replaced the Go to Profile link in the consultant payment request modal
  with an inline bank account form -- consultants with no saved accounts
  can now add one without leaving the dashboard; on save the account is

feat(telegram): add Redis persistence, wire up mainnet + encryption

Every user's wallet record was stored in a local JSON file with no
Redis/KV backend configured on the live bot - Railway containers don't
persist local disk across redeploys, so every user's custodial key was
at risk of being wiped on the next deploy or restart, independent of
the plaintext-storage issue fixed earlier.

Added a Redis (REDIS_URL) backend to store.js, prioritized over the
existing Upstash REST option, so persistence doesn't require a new
third-party account - a standard Railway Redis plugin works directly.
Verified against the actual provisioned instance via `railway run`
(round-trip through the real database, not a mock).

Railway env vars for the live bot (gregarious-vision/beni) also
updated: BENI_NETWORK=Mainnet, BLOCKFROST_MAINNET_KEY, and a fresh
BENI_ENCRYPTION_KEY - the last one is required for the previous
encryption-at-rest commit to work at all; without it every /newwallet
or /importkey call would throw.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(telegram+landing): encrypt custodial keys at rest, sharpen hero copy

The bot stored every user's custodial agent private key in plaintext,
in either Redis or a local JSON file - its own wallet.js comment
already warned "never reuse this custodial model with mainnet funds."
Added crypto.js (AES-256-GCM, key from BENI_ENCRYPTION_KEY) and wired
it transparently into store.js's getUser/setUser, so bot.js and
wallet.js need no changes. Legacy plaintext records pass through
unchanged on read and get encrypted on the next write, so existing
records self-heal without a migration script. Verified round-trip,
legacy passthrough, tamper rejection, and missing-key failure.

Landing hero copy led with "guardrails for institutional AI wallets" -
abstract and easy to skip past. Replaced with the concrete claim: even
a compromised AI, a leaked key, or a buggy app can't cross the limit,
because it's enforced by the ledger, not a policy or a promise.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(mainnet): redeploy agent wallet under the FreezeWallet fix

The flagship demo wallet is redeployed on mainnet under the fixed
validator (tx 56a55cd9...). The previous deployment used the pre-fix
FreezeWallet logic and stays live only as a historical record — the
landing page FAQ now links both, labeled accordingly.

BENI_SCRIPT_ADDRESS and BENI_THREAD_TOKEN_POLICY in Vercel production
also needed updating to the new deployment: they were 9 days stale,
still pointing at the old Preview-testnet demo wallet even after
BENI_NETWORK was set to Mainnet, so the agent-state endpoint had
silently been querying mainnet Blockfrost for a testnet address.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(security): sync FreezeWallet fix into the public /api/deploy endpoint

api/deploy.js is the actual production path every visitor hits when they
connect a wallet and deploy their own guarded agent wallet through the
dashboard - it takes payerAddress, perTxCapLovelace, and dailyCapLovelace
from the caller and sets agentPkh from their own connected wallet, so it
was already correctly built to serve any user's own wallet, not a single
hardcoded one.

But it carries its own separate copy of the compiled validator bytecode,
independent from sdk/src/validators.ts. That copy was never updated after
the FreezeWallet fix, so every real user deploying through the public
dashboard would have silently received the old, pre-fix contract with no
error surfaced anywhere. Synced it from the rebuilt plutus.json.

Added scripts/check-validator-bytecode-sync.mjs + a CI step that fails
if either copy drifts from plutus.json again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(cli+docs): simple flyway command, easy install, payment option

feat(cli+docs): simple `flyway` command, easy install, payment option

Two things a first-time visitor needs: a CLI that isn't a mouthful, and
(for Builder Pie) a way to pay.

Simple invocation + easy install
- `pnpm setup` — one command: install, build, and link `flyway` +
  `flyway-mcp` onto PATH (via npm link). After it, `flyway status` works
  from anywhere instead of `node packages/cli/dist/bin/flyway.js status`.
- Root now depends on flyway-cli/flyway-mcp (workspace:*), so without a
  global link you can still run `pnpm flyway <cmd>` / `pnpm flyway-mcp`
  in-repo (node_modules/.bin is wired).
- scripts/postbuild.mjs chmods the built bins 0755 so the global link
  survives rebuilds (tsc --build drops the +x bit; root build now runs it).
- README / AGENTS.md / index.html quickstarts use the short `flyway`
  form with a `pnpm`-prefix fallback noted.

Payment option (Builder Pie)
- Buy Me a Coffee (pay-what-you-want) added to the README (top bar +
  Support section), the presentation (support button, payment row in the
  walkthrough, verification-checklist item), and the site footer.
- Reconciled the old "payment: none / not a paywall" copy: the protocol
  stays free & MIT; support funds the work without gating a tool.

  shipped, Tiers 6-7) or exit-aware reads "not yet modelled" (shipped at

  remain — those stay marked pending because they genuinely are.
- flyway_discover description now notes HTTPS-URL directories (v0.2a),
  not "v0.1 reads a local directory file" only.
- HTML status snapshot: five -> eight walkthroughs; adds the reach +
  exit-aware paragraph; SHA 17f9bc1 -> 0af2e32 (header, footer).
- .md frontmatter code-sha d5ad56f -> 0af2e32, date -> 2026-07-16.

Styling untouched — both twins already conform to the brand system
(brand.css tokens, self-hosted fonts, theme-toggle). Conceptual content
and diagrams unchanged; only stale status prose + metadata corrected.
